target_schema.name: unified_clinical
target_schema.title: Unified Clinical Data Package (Synthea + OMOP CDM)

conflicts.description: The core demographic entity is named 'patients' in synthea but 'person' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to the target resource 'person'; synthea.patients.id and omop.person.person_id are grouped as the target person_id primary key.

conflicts.description: The clinical contact entity is 'encounters' in synthea versus 'visit_occurrence'/'visit_detail' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Merged into the target resource 'encounter'; OMOP's finer-grained visit_detail hierarchy is preserved as a separate child resource.

conflicts.description: The facility entity is 'organizations' in synthea versus 'care_site' in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to the target resource 'care_site'.

conflicts.description: Synonym column naming: synthea.providers.name / speciality versus omop.provider.provider_name / specialty_source_value.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned to provider_name and specialty_source_value; misspelling 'speciality' corrected.

conflicts.description: Synonym patterns: synthea uses generic 'code'/'description' while OMOP uses '<domain>_source_value'/'<domain>_concept_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Mapped synthea 'code' to the target '<domain>_code' (aligned to OMOP *_source_value) and synthea 'description' to '<domain>_description'.

conflicts.description: Synonym patterns: synthea uses 'start'/'stop'; OMOP uses '<domain>_start_date'/'<domain>_end_date'.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned synthea start/stop to the target start_date/end_date columns per domain.

conflicts.description: synthea.imaging_studies uses human-readable column names containing spaces; the target requires snake_case.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to snake_case (body_site_code, sop_code, modality_code, etc.).

conflicts.description: Monetary amounts are typed as string (synthea and OMOP cost) rather than numeric in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized monetary columns to the Frictionless 'number' type in the target.

conflicts.description: OMOP declares inconsistent types: an identifier typed as date, a name typed as integer, and a concept-id typed as number.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected types in the target: identifiers and concept-ids to string; descriptive names to string.

conflicts.description: synthea.observations.type ('text or numeric') is declared as number although it is a categorical data-type indicator.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to string in the target.

conflicts.description: OMOP '*_datetime' columns are declared as 'date' although they carry time-of-day precision.
conflicts.resolution: Retyped to the Frictionless 'datetime' type in the target.

conflicts.description: Integer-like counters are typed as string in the sources.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized count/utilization columns to 'integer' in the target.

conflicts.description: synthea encounter start/stop are described as 'date and time' but typed as 'date'.
conflicts.resolution: Retained date precision on start_date/end_date; OMOP datetime variants are carried on dedicated start_datetime/end_datetime columns.

conflicts.description: Gender is encoded as 'm'/'f' in synthea versus source value plus standard concept id in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to gender_source_value, with gender_concept_id retained for standardized coding.

conflicts.description: Units are free text in synthea versus source value + standardized unit concept in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Unified to unit_source_value; unit_concept_id retained for standardized units.

conflicts.description: synthea stores raw SNOMED-CT/RxNorm/LOINC/CVX codes; OMOP stores the same as *_source_value paired with a mapped *_source_concept_id.
conflicts.resolution: Unified the raw code into '<domain>_code' (equivalent to *_source_value) and kept separate '<domain>_source_concept_id' columns for OMOP mapping.

conflicts.description: synthea stores a single full birth date; OMOP stores a birth datetime plus decomposed year/month/day components.
conflicts.resolution: Birth date unified to birth_date (grouping birthdate and birth_datetime); decomposed OMOP components retained as distinct columns.

conflicts.description: synthea records a single encounter/line-item cost inline; OMOP records detailed, decomposed cost components in a dedicated cost table.
conflicts.resolution: synthea inline cost retained as an event-level 'cost' attribute; OMOP's normalized cost components retained in the 'cost' resource. Flagged as a residual denormalization.

conflicts.description: Encounter class is a free-text categorical (ambulatory/emergency/…) in synthea versus a standardized visit concept in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Retained encounter_class as a categorical attribute and visit_concept_id as the standardized counterpart.

conflicts.description: Marital status exists only in synthea with no OMOP equivalent.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as a person-level attribute with provenance restricted to synthea.

conflicts.description: synthea is a flat, denormalized clinical schema; OMOP is a normalized CDM with standardized vocabulary and era tables.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the normalized OMOP-style structure as the global skeleton, absorbing synthea attributes into the analogous entities.

conflicts.description: Addresses are embedded inline in synthea entities but normalized into a shared location resource referenced by FK in OMOP.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized all addresses into the 'location' resource; person, care_site and provider reference it via location_id.

conflicts.description: synthea carries inline reasoncode/reasondescription pairs; OMOP expresses reasons through standardized concept foreign keys.
conflicts.resolution: Retained synthea reason_code/reason_description as source attributes; OMOP concept columns preserved separately.

conflicts.description: Era (aggregated time-span) entities exist only in OMOP with no synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as dedicated target resources (condition_era, drug_era, dose_era).

conflicts.description: OMOP's standardized vocabulary/reference tables have no synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as standalone target resources retaining their native structure and FKs.

conflicts.description: synthea has clinical event tables (immunizations, allergies, imaging studies, care plans) with no directly named OMOP entity.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as dedicated target resources (immunization, allergy, imaging_study, care_plan) rather than forcing lossy remapping.

conflicts.description: OMOP models a two-level visit hierarchy (visit_occurrence → visit_detail) while synthea exposes a single flat encounter table.
conflicts.resolution: Encounter unified to encounter; the visit_detail child level retained as a separate resource referenced by encounter.

conflicts.description: synthea encounters are a flat 1-level list; OMOP defines a 1:N parent/child relationship between visit_occurrence and visit_detail.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled encounter as the parent and visit_detail as a 1:N child via visit_occurrence_id FK.

conflicts.description: OMOP episode nests sub-episodes (self-reference) and links to events 1:N via episode_event; synthea has no equivalent.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved episode (with episode_parent_id self-reference) and episode_event bridge as separate resources.

conflicts.description: Death is 1:1 with the person; synthea encodes it inline (deathdate) while OMOP uses a separate death table keyed by person_id.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled death as a separate 1:1 resource keyed by person_id; synthea deathdate mapped to death.death_date.

conflicts.description: Hierarchical and directional concept links form N:M relationships not expressible in a flat entity.
conflicts.resolution: Retained concept_ancestor and concept_relationship as association/bridge resources.

conflicts.description: A person can have multiple overlapping payer plan periods (1:N), with no synthea counterpart.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved payer_plan_period as a 1:N child of person.

conflicts.description: Provider-to-facility is a many-to-one relationship; synthea names it 'organization' while OMOP names it 'care_site_id'.
conflicts.resolution: Unified both to care_site_id FK referencing care_site.

conflicts.description: OMOP explicitly declares primary keys; most synthea tables declare no primary key (only some, like patients.id, carry an id).
conflicts.resolution: Established explicit primary keys on all target resources, listing the corresponding synthea and OMOP source keys in source_provenance.

conflicts.description: synthea FK columns (patient, encounter, provider) are implicit and undeclared, while OMOP declares them via foreignKeys.
conflicts.resolution: Declared explicit foreign keys in the target (person_id, encounter_id, provider_id, care_site_id) and recorded the synthea and OMOP source columns in provenance.

conflicts.description: Several synthea event tables have no identifier column at all, preventing stable row identity.
conflicts.resolution: Introduced surrogate primary keys (condition_occurrence_id, observation_id, immunization_id, allergy_id, imaging_study_id) for these events.

conflicts.description: OMOP association tables rely on composite/natural keys rather than a single surrogate id.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled composite-key association resources as standalone tables without a single-column primary key.

conflicts.description: OMOP death shares its key with person (person_id) as a 1:1 extension.
conflicts.resolution: death.person_id modeled as both primary key and FK to person, with provenance listing both sources.
